fields.label: kneel ollim
fields.description: The ollim's other body. Where the tall form is a bone-white truncate, the kneel form is the shield: a low, swept, wind-aligned dome that grows where the buried moisture is too thin to fund a tower, which is most places the ollim grows at all. A bone-field usually carries one tower and a scatter of kneels, all one organism's slow children. It casts a hard black crescent of shade a grain animal can live in; a loomma cannot, the shadow is too small. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: oorrik
fields.description: A single oorrik is nothing — a wet-mouthed sliver of a thing barely bigger than the grains it moves through. A mound's worth of them is a different problem: dozens surfacing in the same half-second across ten metres of sand, each one too small to hit and too many to count. Nothing about any one of them is dangerous. That was never the point. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: soorrak
fields.description: A sail-winged giant that nests in the deep dune precisely because nothing alive can afford to walk there. Its sun-face is one sheet of mirror-ceramic, so from below, crossing the white sky, it is nearly invisible except as a moving glare; its shade-face carries the eyes, the vents and the brood pouch. It drinks at the green line or a distant shore and carries the water home in its crop. A soorrak nesting crag is the richest square kilometre of surface in the biome, and its eggs are canteens: a full one is drink in a rigid shell, and a Jawa will cross a horizon for a clutch. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: cryoponics vat
fields.description: A sealed, frost-rimed vat that carries its own bath of cryogenic propane, so the Chill's deep-bed plants can be raised anywhere at all, not only on the liquid floor they came from. The bath is pumped and chilled continuously; if power is cut, the plants lose their cold and die back to whatever the room allows. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: Chill floor growing bed
fields.description: A plain steel growing bed for the Chill's deep-bed plants, built to be laid on the frozen seabed where the cold already does the rest. It needs no power, and it can be built nowhere else. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: pillar arm
fields.description: A slab of bone-cored meat as thick as a thigh, hanging to the knee and ending in a knuckled club with no fingers at all. It hits harder than anything a pawn can otherwise grow, and it makes the hand useless for work. It is fed from the body that carries it. It has its own neural structures and may become dangerous if removed. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: lash
fields.description: A pink rope of muscle three times the length of an arm. It coils on the ground behind the pawn and keeps twitching after the pawn has stopped. It is a fast, weak striker that stuns, and it lashes out at people the owner did not mean to hit. It has its own neural structures and may become dangerous if removed. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: eyeburst
fields.description: Where one eye was, a wet cluster of a dozen mismatched eyes has pushed out, pink and blue and all sizes, blinking out of step. It sees further and aims truer than any eye, and it never stops stinging, never closes and never lets the owner sleep well. It has its own neural structures and may become dangerous if removed. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: caudal spring
fields.description: A coiled, segmented tail of gristle grown out of the base of the spine, folded under itself like a compressed spring and ending in a flat pad. It replaces the spine. It lets the owner leap a long way once a day, and it makes every ordinary step slower and stiffer in the cold. It has its own neural structures and may become dangerous if removed. Cutting it out leaves no spine at all. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: bellows
fields.description: A translucent bladder bulging out of one side of the ribcage, swelling and emptying with every breath, with red fog moving inside it. It breathes better than a lung and can blow out a cloud of blinding smoke, but it takes a great deal of air and food, and it is thin enough that every wound bleeds more. It has its own neural structures and may become dangerous if removed. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: pillar arm
fields.description: A slab of bone-cored meat, grown from monstrous tissue inside a Contagion amoeba. Fitted at the shoulder, it replaces the whole arm and hand with a club that hits harder than any hand. It is not matched to anyone, and cutting it out later has consequences. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: lash
fields.description: A pink rope of muscle, grown from monstrous tissue inside a Contagion amoeba. Fitted at the shoulder, it replaces the whole arm and hand with a fast striker that stuns. It is not matched to anyone, and cutting it out later has consequences. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: install grown arm
fields.description: Install a biological arm gestated inside a Contagion amoeba. It is not a device -- it restores the limb itself. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: install grown leg
fields.description: Install a biological leg gestated inside a Contagion amoeba. It is not a device -- it restores the limb itself. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: flood-born
fields.description: Hatched from eggs that waited years in the dry clay, in the hours after the flood receded. A flood-born irqit lives only as long as the mud stays wet: it breeds once, lays into the clay, and dies where it stands as the ground stiffens. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: raven nettle
fields.description: A jet-black nettle, its stalks bristling with fine barbed hairs that catch on cloth and skin and let go of neither. It grows in thick clumps and hides the ground under it. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.settleWarning: Searing heat and a near total lack of arable land make survival here a challenge. Nothing here pursues, but nothing here forgives a mistake either.
fields.label: the Stillsand
fields.description: A corrugated ochre plain under a star that has not moved since the world began, running unbroken to every horizon. Nothing here tracks the sun because the sun does not go anywhere; everything owns a shadow instead, or is buried, or is a giant carrying its own moving shade across a thousand kilometres of nothing. It ends, without a gradient, at a hard green line of river or sea -- and until then, this is the ocean of nothing that line is drawn against. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.endMessage: The dune gale has blown itself out.
fields.letterText:
The windward horizon has gone ochre and every crest is smoking. A dune gale is coming.

For a day or two the dunes will march, the sky will go brown-gold and dim, and the sun will be off you: the one natural relief from the heat out here. The swimmers cannot hear through it either.

But the sand scours anyone left out in it, light walls and roof edges wear, and anything small standing on a crest can be carried away downwind. Keep the light ones off the crests. When it ends, the wind will have uncovered something.
fields.label: dune gale
fields.description: A dune gale is blowing. The dunes are moving, the sun is off, and anything light standing on a crest can be carried downwind. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: dust devil
fields.description: A single spinning column of lifted sand, wandering the flat in fair weather. It lifts anything light, scatters a stockpile and spooks animals, and is gone in minutes. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.letterText:
Something vast is moving under the sand.

The ground is humming on the windward horizon, louder every minute. A krayt dragon is coming, and it is heading for whatever is making the most noise.

It will break the surface and fight. Kill it, or make it dive: it will not stay long on rock, it will not stand in fire, and once it has fed it takes what it caught down with it.
fields.label: krayt attack

fields.letterText:
Something vast is moving under the sand.

At the edge of the map a line of glare is crossing the dunes: a mirror crest, cutting the surface. A muurrok has come up out of the deep sand.

It will weigh everyone it can see and pick the body with the most water in it. If the sun is up it will turn the light off its crest onto that one, then come up underneath it. It takes one body and goes back down.

It cannot follow anyone onto rock for long, and the beam does nothing at night, under a roof, or in a sand gale.
fields.label: muurrok
muurrok
fields.description: A giant that lives under the deep sand and almost never shows itself. All anyone usually sees is its crest: one curved plate polished like a mirror, which breaks the surface as it cruises. It shows up as a line of glare moving across the dunes. It hunts by weighing what it sees. It circles a party at the edge of sight and picks the body with the most water in it. Then it turns the sun on that one, throwing a sweeping beam of reflected light off its crest, and comes up underneath it. It takes one body and goes back down. It ignores everyone else. The beam needs sun. At night, under a roof, or in a sand gale, the crest is just a plate. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: disturbed sand
fields.description: A shallow collapsed funnel ringed with slumped crust. A low furrow runs into it and stops. Something under the sand came up here and took whatever was standing on it. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: drag mark
fields.description: A smeared trough in the sand, scuffed at the edges, with a thin dried smear running down it. Something was pulled under here. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: dune crawler
fields.description: A fist-sized, many-legged scavenger with a fused mineral shell, pulled up out of deep sand on a fishing line. It spends its whole life below the surface filtering decayed organics out of the sand — silverbole leaf-fall, dead things the dune swallowed, whatever a wreck sheds — and only ever reaches the light when something eats it or something catches it. Nothing about it says "fish." Cooked, it eats like a shrimp with regrets. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: rustpuff
fields.description: A large puffball mushroom that bursts at a touch into a cloud of flaky, rust-coloured spores. The spores stain everything and harm nothing; the forest floor is red-brown wherever a herd has walked through a patch. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: qorrax
fields.description: Descended from squid this tentacled monstrosity is like a spider the size of a deer. Fast and aggressive with a lethal bite delivered by venomous beak. An internal shell protects their vital organs. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: brommok timber
fields.description: A massive marsh mushroom with a trunk as hard as wood, rooted in the milk ponds and growing fast enough to see. It cuts into ordinary wood, though not much of it for its size; it will only grow on soft, wet ground. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: Sheen tempest
fields.description: Lightning splits the black sky while the Sheen falls in sheets thick enough to matter — a downpour of spores and fluid that drowns fire as fast as the bolts can start it. Nothing dry survives this uncovered. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: Sheen mist
fields.description: A heavy, glossy mist of settling Sheen hangs at head height, thick enough to blur aim and slow every step. It beads on skin and gear alike. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: Sheen-fall
fields.description: The Rot's own reproductive sleet, cloying and glossy, falling in place of rain. It slicks every surface and douses open flame same as any downpour — it is wet, it is simply never water. Anything left uncovered beneath it comes away coated. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: sikkra lure
fields.description: Tiny caps that light up a cold teal in the dark to draw small prey, which lands, sticks to the gills and is slowly digested. Whole swarms of gnats die to a single patch; the light is the trap. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: rukka cap
fields.description: A damp-ground mushroom with a cap wrinkled like a walnut, glowing a soft lilac from the folds. It is the grazers' staple; anything that eats fungus eats this first. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: churrun mast
fields.description: A mast of pale fungus standing in the milk ponds, lit from inside with a cold blue-green light. It grows fast and cuts into mushroom logs, though not many; mostly it is the thing you steer by across the shallows. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: mycelial soil
fields.description: Soil with mycelium spread throughout. It's kind of ugly and takes a lot of work to build, but it's perfect for growing darkness-loving crops. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: mycelial matting
fields.description: Rough mycelium matting for use in animal barns where straw is unavailable. It is cheap and accepts very little filth. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: the Sheen's breath
fields.description: The Rot's own reproductive cycle never truly pauses here — even between Sheen-falls, its spores hang thin in the air, ready to seed anyone who lingers unroofed too long. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes
